name: Bacha Khan International Airport
before:
Pakistan's fourth busiest airport, at the south western end of Peshawar, and unusual in that around 75 per cent of its flights are international. It serves the north west of the country and the adjoining areas of Afghanistan.

The runway has a genuine curiosity attached to it. One of the main runways is crossed by a railway line, the Khyber train safari, which runs up to Landi Kotal in the Khyber Pass for tourists. It is one of very few runways in the world crossed by a railway, though the line is rarely operational.

The runway itself is 9,000 feet and rated ICAO category 4E, taking aircraft up to a 777-300ER, with nose-in parking for four wide bodies at a time and two air bridges added in 2018.

Islamabad is about 180 km away, roughly two hours on the M-1 motorway.

The airport was extensively reconstructed between 2016 and 2018 and renamed in January 2012 after Abdul Ghaffar Khan, known as Bacha Khan, the Pashtun nationalist leader.
after:
Bacha Khan International is Peshawar's airport, at the south western end of the city. The FCDO advises against all travel to Peshawar, including the city of Peshawar, and warns that travelling against its advice could invalidate travel insurance.

Traffic here is mostly international, and the airport serves Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province in the north west of the country. Its single runway is about 2,700 metres long.

claims.note: Was 'unusual in that around 75 per cent of its flights are international'. Wikipedia gives 75 per cent of flights; the Airports Authority's 2025 figures give 1.06 million of 1.29 million passengers (about 82 per cent). Both support 'mostly international'; neither percentage is quoted because the two measure different things. 'Unusual' is opinion.

claims.why: Good sources disagree. Wikipedia says fourth busiest. The Airports Authority's 2025 figures (ProPakistani, 16 Feb 2026) put Multan (1.365 million international plus 80,000 domestic) ahead of Peshawar (1.29 million), which makes it fifth. Not split, cut.

claims.why: The Afghanistan part rests on Wikipedia alone; the FCDO now advises against all travel within 10 miles of the Afghan border. The north west is kept, above.
